text:
Judge Michael Rasmussen by the scoresheet and you'd wonder why he plays 16 minutes a night: one goal and four points in 18 games. Look at what happens when he's on the ice and the picture flips. At five on five, Detroit gets 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances, for and against) with him out there. The Red Wings have scored 10.9 fewer goals than those chances deserve with him on, and he has one goal on 3.95 expected of his own.

The Detroit Free Press wrote that he and J.T. Compher are "playing up to Detroit Red Wings' standard at last," and the underlying numbers back that up. The 6'6" center blocks shots (28 already), kills penalties and profiles like Ridly Greig or Eetu Luostarinen.

What he doesn't do is create much himself. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking found his value isn't built on five-on-five offense, and Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, so the upside is modest. But 3.7% shooting won't hold, and when the bounces even out we'd expect his points to look more like his play. Our range has him at 7 to 16 goals this season.
headline: Michael Rasmussen's line deserves better than this
